correctness.rationale: For nonempty triangle-free H, direct four-clique enumeration gives an exact simplicial union B=(full simplex on H)*D_A, Y=Ind(H)*E_A union T_A, intersection Z=Ind(H)*D_A. B is contractible and inclusion is cofibrant, so X is homotopy equivalent to Y/Z. Each of the binomial(m,2) edge blocks is the cofiber of the suspension of Ind(H) inside a contractible join, hence a double suspension. Their intersections vanish in Z. The residual binomial(m,3) triangles attach via loops in a simply connected wedge and contribute free 2-spheres. The proof covers all m>=2 and finite nonempty triangle-free H, including disconnected H; no finite-experiment extrapolation. The independently constructed verifier checked every labeled triangle-free H on <=5 vertices with m=2,3,4, plus four six-vertex graphs, comprising 1329 instances, 3987 field homology checks, and a counterexample to omitting triangle-freeness.

value.rationale: The result relates two distinct natural graph-associated simplicial complexes by an integral homotopy equivalence valid for every nonempty triangle-free graph and all clique sizes m>=2. It is a structural realization tool: taking m=2 exactly double-suspends the independence complex, and Barmak/Jonsson bipartite realization then yields CF4 examples realizing arbitrary triple suspensions and prescribed torsion in higher degrees. The explicit m=3, H=C5 example gives S^2 wedge three S^3, a mixed-dimensional classification. The sharp triangle-containing counterexample shows a genuine structural boundary. These are motivated universal homotopy consequences, not a small-parameter recomputation.
